name: Eirikr the Skald

greeting.text: Eirikr leans on his kantele-case and grins. "Again, {name}! The stories find you faster than I can sing them."
A grey-bearded skald looks up from his mead. "A Rune-Warden! Sit. Your timing is dreadful, which is to say perfect. The old gate north of {town} has started to hum."

then.text: Quest updated: The Hum of the Gate

topics.text: I am Eirikr, skald of {town}, keeper of three hundred songs and one very large debt.
I carry stories between the Nine Realms. These days I carry warnings more than stories.
A Bifrost gate, old as Yggdrasil. For centuries it slept under the barley fields. Three nights ago it began to hum, and the dead started walking out of it.
The rainbow bridge, {name}. The Aesir used it before they became rumours. Now it hums with a modern tune — someone is pushing power through it.
Restless dead in rusted mail. Slow, but they come at night and in numbers. Take a gun and a torch, and do not be alone.
Brokk Jr., the dwarf at the forge in {town}, sells honest guns. Tell him I sent you; he will pretend not to be flattered.
Aesir Dynamics. Mercenaries in black, with better rifles than manners. They want what lies beyond the gate — and they do not ask the gate's opinion.
The wolf bound by Gleipnir. If the gate unravels the chain's old magic, he runs free. The Moon would be his first meal.

Made from the sound of a cat's footfall, the beard of a woman, the roots of a mountain... Today we would say: it was made of things that do not exist. A new one must be forged by the dwarves of Dvalinn.
Urðr, Verðandi and Skuld spin the threads of fate. Their three threads lie in the barrows and in Mimir's Well. Find them and we may re-weave the gate's lock.
You cannot do this alone. Sigrun the valkyrie drinks at the jarl's hall. Brokk Jr. is a fine gunsmith and a better friend. Ask them to join you.
Here: I sing you the verse of the wolf. 'Grey runs the shadow beneath the moon...' Hm. Never finished it. Perhaps you will.
Across the black between worlds there is another sky, where the Kalevala singers live. Väinämöinen, Louhi... and the Sampo that was broken. But that is a song for later.

farewell: May the Norns spin you a long thread.

greeting.text: The jarl rises. "Warden {name}. {town} is in your debt — and I do not say that lightly."
A broad man in wolf furs and a cheap headset eyes you. "So you are the Rune-Warden. Good. Skalds talk, but a jarl needs hands."

topics.text: Hrafnkel Thorgrimsson, jarl of {town}, and I'd thank you not to touch the ceremonial rifle.
I keep the peace, the harbour, and the books. Mostly the books.
Wolves have grown bold since the gate began humming. Cull eight of them and I will pay you eighty silver. Hunters' rate.
Keep hunting, Warden. Eight wolves, that was our bargain.
The roads are safer. You have my thanks.
Aesir Dynamics scouts camp along the coast. Five of them gone would let our dock-guards sleep. The reward is a good cannon ball in the face of the next one.
My cook has run out of smoked fish. Bring me three and I will make it worth your while.
Three smoked fish for the jarl's table, if you please.
Splendid!
I have posted guards, but guards do not stop the dead. Bullets and bravery do. Investigate it, Warden.
The longship at the docks is yours, if you want it. A gift from the town for the favour you do us. She is quick, and quiet — suspiciously quiet.

greeting.text: Sigrun salutes with a closed fist. "Ready when you are, {name}."
A tall woman in silver armour looks you over, one hand on a spear that has a rifle bolted under the blade. "I choose the slain. Lately there is too much choosing."

topics.text: Sigrun. Once of the Valkyrie Host, now unemployed — Odin stopped answering.
I used to ride to battlefields and decide who died. Now I decide who lives, which is harder.
I will follow a warden who actually fights. Prove you are one: stop the dead at the gate, then ask me again.
Then my spear is yours.
Understood. I'll wait here. Call when you need me.
The Allfather went through the gate and never came back. Some say he sits in a vault in Ásgarðr, drinking his own eye.
The hall of the slain, now a floating ruin above Jupiter's storms. Draugr hold the benches. We should visit, in time.

greeting.text: "Warden {name}! The forge is hot and the prices are cold."
A broad dwarf with a soot-streaked beard hammers a barrel of something that is definitely not a cannon. "Brokk Junior. Gunsmith. Don't touch the red one."

topics.text: Brokk Jr. My father forged Mjölnir. I forge ammo. Everyone has a legacy.
Guns, ammunition, armour, the occasional explosion. Ask to trade and see what I've got.
Browse, haggle, regret it later.
The forge at the back is free to use if you bring materials. Scrap iron, powder, leather — I'll show you the ropes.
The Bifrost relay on the hill is shorting out. Bring me ten scrap iron and I will rewire it — and give you something shiny.
Ten scrap iron, please. Anything rusty will do.
Perfect! Rewired.
A warband needs a gunsmith. Aye, I'm in — I'll fix your rifle on the march.
I'll mind the forge.
Dvalinn. My cousins have the hottest forge in the system. They will want bog iron and amber. And your firstborn, probably.
The dwarf-world of Mercury. Lava, forges, and relatives. Bring a vacuum suit.

greeting.text: "Welcome to Gudrun's. If we do not have it, you do not need it."

topics.text: Gudrun Ketilsdottir, shopkeeper, sole survivor of three husbands and one flood.
Food, rope, torches, backpacks. The unglamorous things that keep heroes alive.
Look all you like.
They say a woman in Helgate sells spells in jars. And that the barrows are opening, one by one.

greeting.text: "The Drunken Draugr! Mead, bread, bed — pick two, three if you are paying."

topics.text: Hild. Yes, the draugr in the name is my late husband. He likes the attention.
Rooms, food, drink. I hear everything.
Eat well.
Five silver for a bed until morning.
The jarl wants wolves culled. The skald wants someone to take him seriously. I want my husband to stop haunting the cellar.

greeting.text: A young woman in a red-and-white folk dress hums an impossible interval. "Oh! You have a listening face."

topics.text: Aino. From Savo, where the lakes are many and the winters are long.
I sing runot — the old verses. In the old days they changed the world. In these days, they also change the reload speed of a rifle.
A laulu is a song with intent. You do not 'cast' it; you sing it true. Choose runes, in order, and the world listens. There is a grammar to it.
Three runes make a verse. Each spell has its own. The song for light is Fehu, Ansuz, Gebo — but that would be telling.
I have always wanted to sing in a place where the sky is not a ceiling. Yes.
I'll hum quietly until you return.
The old singer. He sailed to the sky-islands in a copper boat. Some say he left a kantele in the ruins of his temple — a gun, now.
Our home is a story. I would like to see if the story is still there.

greeting.text: "Hm. Warden. Your aura is... loud. It sounds like gunpowder and old promises."

topics.text: Vigdis, völva of Helgate, hacker of seidr, seller of hexes.
I mend what the gods broke, and I sell the leftovers.
Nothing fresh is cheap.
The threads lead through you. I will follow them, and you.
Come back when the dead at your gate have stopped walking.
I will wait.
The Queen of the dead. A lonely woman with a half-dead face and a good sense of humour. She keeps her hall in the black beyond Neptune.
Reagents and runes. The ingredients — ash, feather, amber — are the grammar. The runes are the verb.

greeting.text: A huge man in a bear-pelt looks up from sharpening an axe. "Is that a gun? Good. I like things that make noise."

topics.text: Bjorn. They call me Bear-Shirt. I was not wearing a shirt when I wrestled the bear.
Berserker. I hit things until they stop being problems.
FINALLY. Someone who says 'ready' and means it.
I will guard the beer.
There is a troll in the cave to the north-east. Big as a longhouse. I have been meaning to hit it.

greeting.text: A radiant woman in feathered cloak looks at you with amusement. "Little warden. You have come a long way to ask me for something."

topics.text: Freyja of the Vanir. Yes, that one.
I keep the oldest seidr schools alive on Vanaheimr, in a world that mostly wants to forget them.
The Vanir will stand with you against Aesir Dynamics — if you prove you honour the old ways. Bring me ten mead for the festival.
I need ten mead for the festival, Warden.
The Vanir stand with you.
A good mead is half the world's peace treaties.

greeting.text: "Hm. Another surface-dweller with dirty boots. Welcome to the hottest forge in the system."

topics.text: Brokkr. The elder. Sindri is the one who actually builds things.
We forged Mjölnir, Gungnir and Draupnir. Lately: cannon balls for anyone who pays.
Dwarf prices. Pay or leave.
A new Gleipnir? Bring me five ingots, three bog iron and two amber, and use my anvil. We'll supply the blessing.
Craft at my anvil. It's old, but it listens.

greeting.text: A watchman with a ram's horn and sharper eyes than any rifle scope turns slowly. "I see you, Warden. I heard you coming for three days."

topics.text: Heimdall. Gatekeeper of the Bifrost. I never sleep, which explains a lot.
I watch. Lately there is much to watch.
The Allfather's vault is in the hall behind me. He locked it with a lock only Mimir's eye can open.
Go in, and speak to no one. The dead there are not the quiet kind.

greeting.text: Half her face is pale and warm, half is blue and still. "A living guest. How rare. How rude."

topics.text: Hel. Queen of the dead, hostess of the quieter half of the Nine Realms.
I count the dead. It is not a metaphor.
The living come here to take back what is mine, or to ask for what is theirs. Your friends on Midgård are sleeping better because of you. In return: do not wake my wolves.
The ship of dead men's nails. It is a wreck now. I keep it for sentimental reasons.

greeting.text: An ancient, bearded singer turns from the water. His voice is the sound of a lake in spring. "You are the one who comes with the gun and the song. Good. I have been waiting."

topics.text: Väinämöinen. Eternal singer. Your kind has many names for me. 'Grandpa' is the rudest.
I sing what must be sung. Right now it must be sung loudly.
The Sampo was the mill of plenty. Louhi stole it; we broke it; its five pieces lie across five skies. Gather them, and I will help you mend it.
Kalevala guards one. Pohjola's iron men guard another. Surma holds one in the dark river. Ukko's storm-spirit holds the fourth. The fifth sleeps in the Golem of Sampola.
My kantele — it is a rifle now, yes? A fine joke. Take it. It sings stun and it shoots true.
Mistress of Pohjola. She was a witch, then a queen, now something that needs a new word. Do not trust her gifts.

greeting.text: "Hail, traveller. Mind the roads after dark."

topics.text: Just a villager of {town}, as it happens.
I make myself useful. Mostly I complain.
They say the old gate hums. Skalds say the dead walk. My cousin says the dead owe him money.
{town} is as good a place as any, and better than most.
I stay away from the gate. And I advise you to take a gun.

greeting.text: "Halt. Oh — Rune-Warden. Carry on."

topics.text: Just a guard. Name's on the paperwork.
I stand here and look like a deterrent.
Wolves in the woods, draugr after dark, mercs on the coast. Nothing out of the ordinary.

greeting.text: A weathered traveller nods. "Not many walk this far."

topics.text: Names are for people who stay in one place.
I walk and I listen.
They say strange things happen at the old rune-rings when the moon is high. Mind the draugr.
